summary: CORRECTS the SEC-L1 row recorded at 2026-11-07T11:48:06Z. The claim 'back-to-back unpaged calls can starve ingest (about 950 ms in a five-call burst)' is WRONG for the real path: it came from a loop calling only the accessor, where std::mutex lets the reader re-take the lock before a woken writer runs. Through list_devices() the registry phase (about 650 ms) separates the accessor calls, and a five-call burst gave a worst heartbeat upsert of 216-234 ms, about one call. MEASURED at 500k agents on the real store with the shipped accessor logic (the two production files compiled -O2 into a throwaway bench, 30 tags per agent, idle 32-core box, one writer thread; the vcpkg libraries are debug builds, so the rest of the binary is not representative): registry to_json_obj() 630-650 ms (max 780), guardian_backend_for(all) 150-170 ms, list_devices() total about 1.0 s, existing 15 s sweep 1.15-1.3 s. The dominant fleet-scale cost of an unpaged read is the PRE-EXISTING registry lock hold in to_json_obj(): a concurrent registry get_session blocked 0.6-1.1 s per list_devices() call (isolated to_json_obj alone: 1.0-1.1 s worst). This branch neither causes nor changes it. Four of the six list_devices() callers discard the new field (server.cpp and software_catalogue_model.cpp use only .size(); crypto_api.cpp reads hostnames; the dashboard fragment is barred from carrying the field) and still pay the lookup. The health-lock part is mitigated in 67c7185ce (see UP-2). STILL DEFERRED: the registry to_json_obj hold, a connected_count(), paging, and an opt-in so the four discarding callers skip the lookup. Author-run, not reviewed by any agent or model.

CORRECTS and supersedes the UP-2 row recorded at 2026-11-07T11:48:07Z (same wrong 950 ms burst figure; see SEC-L1). Mitigated in 67c7185ce: guardian_backend_for takes mu_ per 4096 ids (kGuardianBackendSlice) and sleeps 50 us between slices (kGuardianBackendPause). Prototype results at 500k, worst concurrent heartbeat upsert, single writer: unsliced 180-230 ms; 4096-id slices alone 185-230 ms (no help: the reader re-takes the mutex first); slices plus yield() 180-290 ms (no help); slices plus 50 us sleep 2-4 ms, for about 10 ms more per call (accessor median 150 -> 165-172 ms). The pause is load-bearing and its constant says so. Not measured on the committed code itself (the bench used a patched copy of the same logic, with the pause after the slice instead of before the next), not run under TSan, and the field is read per slice rather than from one snapshot, which list_devices never was either. Tests in 67c7185ce: slice-boundary alignment (red when the slice end is off by one, checked by mutation) and a concurrent writer-versus-reader case. Author-run, not reviewed by any agent or model.
